claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately captures the prohibition against a driver using alcohol or being under the influence of alcohol within 4 hours before going on duty, operating, or having physical control of a commercial motor vehicle pursuant to paragraph (a)(1).

The claim accurately represents paragraph (a)(2), prohibiting drivers from using alcohol, being under the influence of alcohol, or having any measured alcohol concentration or detected presence of alcohol while on duty, operating, or in physical control of a commercial motor vehicle.

The claim accurately states the prohibition in paragraph (a)(3) barring a driver from being on duty or operating a commercial motor vehicle while possessing specified alcoholic beverages, including the referenced statutory definitions and exceptions.
The claim correctly reflects paragraph (b)(1), prohibiting a motor carrier from requiring or permitting a driver to violate any provision of paragraph (a).

The claim accurately states paragraph (b)(2), prohibiting a motor carrier from requiring or permitting a driver to be on duty or operate a commercial motor vehicle if the driver appears to have used alcohol within the preceding four hours.
The claim accurately conveys paragraph (c), requiring that any driver found in violation of paragraph (a) or (b) be placed out-of-service immediately for 24 hours.
The claim correctly reflects paragraph (c)(1), stating that the 24-hour out-of-service period commences upon issuance of an out-of-service order.
The claim accurately states paragraph (c)(2), prohibiting drivers from violating the terms of an out-of-service order issued under this section.
The claim correctly captures paragraph (d)(1), requiring a driver issued an out-of-service order under this section to report its issuance to their employer within 24 hours.

The claim accurately conveys paragraph (d)(2), including both the baseline 30-day reporting obligation to the designated State official and the alternative timing rule following affirmation upon administrative review.

The claim accurately states the first sentence of paragraph (e), entitling a driver subject to an out-of-service order to petition for review in writing within 10 days of issuance to the Division Administrator or State Director.
The claim accurately captures the authority granted in the second sentence of paragraph (e) allowing the Division Administrator or State Director to affirm or reverse the order.
The claim correctly conveys the third sentence of paragraph (e), permitting any driver adversely affected by the order to petition the Administrator for review under 49 CFR 386.13.
The claim accurately represents paragraph (a)(3)(i), providing an exception to the possession prohibition for alcoholic beverages manifested and transported as part of a shipment.
The claim accurately represents paragraph (a)(3)(ii), providing an exception to the possession prohibition for alcoholic beverages possessed or used by bus passengers.

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 completely and faithfully retains the prohibition against alcohol use or influence within 4 hours prior to operating or going on duty.

Claim C0013 explicitly retains the exception for manifested and transported shipments.
Claim C0014 explicitly retains the exception for alcohol possessed or used by bus passengers.
Claim C0003 fully retains the prohibition against motor carriers requiring or permitting a driver to violate paragraph (a).
Claim C0004 fully retains the prohibition on motor carriers requiring or permitting a driver who appears to have used alcohol within the past 4 hours to be on duty or operate.
Claim C0005 fully retains the requirement to immediately place a violating driver out-of-service for 24 hours.
Claim C0006 fully retains the provision governing the commencement of the 24-hour out-of-service period upon issuance of the order.
Claim C0007 fully retains the prohibition against violating an out-of-service order issued under this section.
Claim C0008 fully retains the duty of the driver to report order issuance to the employer within 24 hours.
Claim C0009 fully retains the requirement to report order issuance to the designated State official within 30 days unless review is requested.
Claim C0009 fully retains the requirement to report to the State official within 30 days of affirmation if the driver requests review.
Claim C0010 fully retains the permission and procedure for a driver to petition for review within 10 days.
Claim C0011 fully retains the authority of the Division Administrator or State Director to affirm or reverse the out-of-service order.
Claim C0012 fully retains the permission for an adversely affected driver to petition the Administrator for review under 49 CFR 386.13.
